item.title: Pentagon Inspector General Details U.S. Losses and Challenges in Iran War
item.author: John Ismay
item.content:encoded: Helicopters for evacuating casualties were pulled from four countries, and hundreds of military facilities were destroyed, according to a new report.

item.title: US Senate Blocks Clarity Act Crypto Bill
item.content:encoded: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Troy Downing (R-MT) says that proposed $5,000 checks could add to the deficit and fuel inflation as he raises concerns about the plan’s price tag. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says that he expects Leon Black will be held in contempt after the House Oversight Committee panel voted to advance the matter to the full House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Approves $2.8 Billion Arms Sale to Israel, Including 40,000 One-Ton Bombs
item.author: Michael Crowley and Edward Wong
item.content:encoded: The package would be among the largest deliveries of U.S. munitions to Israel.

item.title: Trump Plans Blitz of $138 Million and Counting to Save Midterm Republicans
item.author: Theodore Schleifer, Shane Goldmacher and Maggie Haberman
item.content:encoded: His powerful super PAC is suddenly spending heavily on some races, after drawing fire from some Republicans that the group might not throw its weight behind the party’s candidates.

item.title: Rep. Krishnamoorthi Says Leon Black Vote May Be Unanimous
item.content:encoded: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says that he expects Leon Black will be held in contempt after the House Oversight Committee panel voted to advance the matter to the full House. Rep. Krishnamoorthi says that he expects to support the Russia sanctions bill even though it would give President Trump additional tariff authority, arguing that more pressure is needed on Russia’s oil revenues. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Federal Employees Were Paid $9.5 Billion Not to Work in 2025 Under DOGE Effort
item.author: Eileen Sullivan
item.content:encoded: As part of the Department of Government Efficiency’s program to shrink the federal work force, paid administrative leave costs rose by 435 percent.

item.title: Rep. Downing Says Fed Has No Choice But To Raise Rates
item.content:encoded: Rep. Troy Downing (R-MT) says that proposed $5,000 checks could add to the deficit and fuel inflation as he raises concerns about the plan’s price tag. Rep. Downing says that the Federal Reserve has “no choice” but to raise rates with inflation still above target and expects a modest increase. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Melania Trump Encourages Children to Build ‘the Next Great Robot’ With A.I.
item.author: Erica L. Green
item.content:encoded: The first lady, who has been a champion of A.I. during her husband’s second term, said the Mountain View Elementary School students should be at the forefront of technology.

item.title: Crypto’s Push Into Wall Street Suffers Setback After Bill Fails
item.author: Olga Kharif and Scott Patterson
item.content:encoded: Crypto’s long march into mainstream finance took a step backward Tuesday when the Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act, denying the industry a chance to turn its newfound influence in Washington into fresh rules that could outlast the current administration.

item.title: Trump Defended A.I. Data Centers on Truth Social, and Commenters Clapped Back
item.author: Stuart A. Thompson
item.content:encoded: The president’s posts about artificial intelligence on the social media platform he founded were met with an unusual volume of criticism.

item.title: McCarthy Gets a Portrait Marking His Brief, Strange Speakership
item.author: Annie Karni
item.content:encoded: Kevin McCarthy, the first speaker to be ousted from the post, was honored at the Capitol at the unveiling of his official portrait.

item.title: Senate Advances Legislation to Regulate College Sports Landscape
item.author: Janet Lorin and Steven T. Dennis
item.content:encoded: The Senate advanced a bipartisan bill that would attempt to regulate the rapidly-changing world of college sports, in a rush to move the legislation before lawmakers leave Washington for the midterm elections.

item.title: Businessweek Daily: Future Proof Day Special (Podcast)
item.content:encoded:
Wall Street traders refrained from making riskier bets in the countdown to the Federal Reserve decision, with stocks falling as elevated oil prices drove bond yields to multi-year highs. Almost 350 firms in the S&P 500 dropped. Benchmark 10-year yields hit the highest level in nearly two decades. Longer-dated Treasuries extended losses after a weak $13 billion sale of 20-year bonds. Brent crude settled above $108, fueling inflation worries. Bitcoin tumbled as the US Senate blocked a landmark crypto bill in an industry loss.
On today's episode Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec host from a special episode in Huntington Beach, CA:
Tony Davidow, Senior Private Market Strategist, Franklin Templeton Institute Jan van Eck, VanEck Funds CEO Jaime Magyera, Senior Managing Director, Head of U.S. Wealth and Head of Retirement, BlackRock Scott Dennis, Head of ETFs, TCW (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump's Midterm Mail Ballot Curbs
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court refused to clear the Postal Service to enforce new restrictions on mail-in ballots for the congressional midterms, in a rebuff to the Trump administration. Jeff Mason has more on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Iran War Blockade Costs Strain Taiwan China Deterrence
item.author: Gerry Doyle, Becca Wasser, Jen Judson, Courtney McBride and Hayley Warren
item.content:encoded: The cost of naval operations since the buildup began in January has topped $7.1 billion — not including all the US assets being used to escort tankers through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Bond Yields Surge Ahead of the Fed Rate Decision
item.content:encoded: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are DWS Group Head of Fixed Income, Americas George Catrambone, Upwork CEO Hayden Brown, Citizens Equity Research Analyst, Managing Director Jay McCanless, VSORA Chair Sandra Rivera, Rockefeller Global Family Office Private Advisor Angela Mwanza, Oaktree Portfolio Manager Danielle Poli, Wellington Management Private Capital Formation & Investor Relations Head Laura Kirk, Robinhood Futures & Prediction Markets VP & GM JB Mackenzie, MoneyGram CEO Anthony Soohoo, & Dutch Bros CEO & President Christine Barone. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Angela Mwanza Sees 25-Basis-Point Fed Cut
item.content:encoded: Angela Mwanza, Managing Director and Private Advisor at Rockefeller Global Family Office, joined the program to discuss the Federal Reserve outlook ahead of tomorrow’s decision. In response to whether the Fed will act, she said she thinks the central bank is looking at a 25-basis-point move. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Bailey Lipschultz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sheinbaum Tax Change Eyes New Revenue But Businesses Fear Impact
item.author: Alex Vasquez and Gonzalo Soto
item.content:encoded: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum is proposing sweeping changes to corporate income tax rules to raise as much as 140 billion pesos ($8.2 billion) next year, part of an effort to narrow the budget deficit but one that risks squeezing low-margin businesses.

item.title: Robinhood Predictions VP on Growth in Event Contracts
item.content:encoded: JB Mackenzie, Robinhood Futures & Prediction Markets VP & GM, discusses rising trading activity in prediction markets ahead of the Federal Reserve’s rate decision, with markets pricing in an roughly 85% chance of a 25-basis-point hike. He sas interest in Fed-related contracts has grown substantially over the past year, moving from relatively muted early adoption to one of Robinhood’s most popular contracts. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Leon Black Contempt Resolution Advanced by House Epstein Panel
item.author: Caitlin Reilly
item.content:encoded: The House committee investigating disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein voted to recommend holding billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress Tuesday after he defied subpoenas for testimony and documents related to women in Epstein’s orbit.

item.title: House Kills Bid to Impeach Trump as Democrats Split
item.author: Michael Gold
item.content:encoded: Dozens of Democrats declined to register a position on articles of impeachment by one of their own members, Representative Al Green, that cited President Trump’s immigration crackdown.

item.title: ‘60 Minutes’ Season Premiere Sees Dip in Ratings
item.author: Michael M. Grynbaum
item.content:encoded: Just under 8 million people watched Sunday’s season premiere, down 21 percent from last year. Viewership for the N.F.L. lead-in fell by about the same.

item.title: Canada Is a Sleeping Giant Economically, Says Blackstone's Gray
item.content:encoded: Blackstone Inc. President Jon Gray says Canada has massive opportunities to grow due to its natural resources, looser regulatory policies and access to private capital. “Canada is a sleeping giant economically," he said Tuesday at an investment summit in Toronto. (Source: Bloomberg)

Paisley Nardini, Head of Investment Strategy for Tema ETFs, discusses the industry group ETFs that are surging right now as industry leaders gather in Huntington Beach, California for Future Proof. item.title: Independent Budget Office Estimates Iran War Has Cost $38 Billion
item.author: Catie Edmondson
item.content:encoded: The Congressional Budget Office said its analysis had been limited by the fact that the Defense Department did not respond to requests for information on the costs of the conflict.

item.title: Kash Patel Suggests FBI Agents Could Go to Election Polling Sites
item.author: Devlin Barrett
item.content:encoded: Federal law prohibits armed federal officers or military personnel from being deployed to polling stations.

item.title: Crypto Stocks and Tokens Drop After Senate Blocks Landmark Bill
item.author: Lydia Beyoud and Steven T. Dennis
item.content:encoded: Senators from both parties blocked a landmark digital asset market structure bill in a procedural vote Tuesday, sending cryptocurrency stocks tumbling after a major setback for industry.

item.title: Trump Says Kennedy Center Revamp Hinges on Adding His Name
item.author: Jeff Mason
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump threatened to scrap efforts to repair the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts unless his name is added to the building, shortly after his hand-picked board approved a renovation plan.

item.title: Half of Voters Dislike Socialism Amid Progressive Wins, New Poll Finds
item.author: Kellen Browning and Ruth Igielnik
item.content:encoded: Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor and democratic socialist, was viewed more favorably than Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a fellow high-profile member of the movement.

item.title: Supreme Court Stands Up to Trump on Mail Voting and a Few Key Issues
item.author: Adam Liptak
item.content:encoded: The justices take their time and pick their spots, but they have rejected presidential initiatives on tariffs, citizenship, the National Guard — and now the coming election.

item.title: Merz Cancels UN Trip to Address CDU Party Rebellion in Berlin
item.author: Arne Delfs
item.content:encoded: Friedrich Merz cancelled his trip to the United Nations General Assembly in New York next week, changing course as the German chancellor faces growing opposition within his own conservative party ahead of closely-watched regional elections on Sunday.

item.title: A.I. Is Unpopular With Voters, a New York Times/Siena Poll Finds
item.author: Tim Balk and Caroline Soler
item.content:encoded: As fears grow about the threat of artificial intelligence, neither party has claimed an advantage on the technology, a New York Times/Siena poll found. But voters are united in opposition to data centers.

item.title: How the Postal Service Became Central to U.S. Elections
item.author: Dan Watson
item.content:encoded: The mail system took on new prominence during the Civil War by enabling soldiers to vote from afar. On Monday, the Supreme Court blocked President Trump’s effort to give it a new role in elections.

item.title: Congress Has Proposed Many Bills for A.I. Regulation. Lawmakers Have Enacted Few.
item.author: Tony Romm, Dustin Volz and Michael Gold
item.content:encoded: For years, Democrats and Republicans have proposed bills to address the greatest threats posed by artificial intelligence. Many remain stymied by political disputes.

item.title: FEMA Could Still Lose More Jobs Despite Court Ruling
item.author: Scott Dance
item.content:encoded: A plan to halve the agency’s sprawling work force was illegal, a judge ruled. But the court is not blocking other FEMA cuts.

item.title: Trump Slams Supreme Court Over Mail-In Voting Ruling
item.author: Tyler Pager
item.content:encoded: In a blistering attack on the court, President Trump said “these are not the people I interviewed” to serve as justices.

item.title: A ‘Blue Wave’ May Be Building, but How High?
item.author: Nate Cohn
item.content:encoded: A Times/Siena national poll suggests Republicans are reeling. Can they come back by depicting Democrats as too far to the left?

item.title: Brazil Top Court Puts Off Moraes Decision, Clouding Election
item.author: Daniel Carvalho, Martha Beck and Beatriz Reis
item.content:encoded: Brazil’s Supreme Court delayed a decision on whether to open an unprecedented investigation into one of its justices after a tense public hearing in which members traded accusations of political bias and spreading falsehoods about each other.

item.title: U.S. Has Deployed Weapons in Space, Air Force Secretary Says
item.author: Francesca Regalado
item.content:encoded: Troy E. Meink’s comments were the first public acknowledgment of American weapons in orbit. The Pentagon has been preparing for potential conflict in space with Russia or China.

item.title: Hong Kong Leader to Unveil Five-Year Plan That Outlasts His Term
item.author: Nectar Gan
item.content:encoded: Hong Kong leader John Lee is taking the unprecedented step of outlining a five-year vision for the Asian financial hub. The question is whether he’ll be the chief executive to see it through.

item.title: With Trump’s Plans Blocked, States Work to Restore Trust in Mail Voting
item.author: Nick Corasaniti, Anna Griffin and Richard Fausset
item.content:encoded: President Trump’s efforts to restrict mail voting ahead of the midterms were thwarted by the Supreme Court, but they have sowed confusion and doubt among some voters.

item.title: Democrats Gain Midterms Edge as Trump Drags Down Republicans, Per Times/Siena Poll
item.author: Shane Goldmacher, Ruth Igielnik and Sophia June
item.content:encoded: Even some Republicans are losing faith in Trump’s economy, a New York Times/Siena poll found, and Democrats were favored on the top issues as the sprint to the midterms gets underway.
